thread:
Maria: quick heads-up  the new inline onboarding banner is causing the page to jump on mobile when it appears. users lose their scroll position in the sample projects list and keyboard users end up below the fold.
Dylan: hmm that's bad. is it because we're inserting the banner at the top and changing layout height?
Maria: yep. we prepend it right under the header which pushes content down; on long pages mobile chrome keeps the visual viewport but keyboard focus moves relative to DOM and lands mid-list.
Noor: I saw this in a user test earlier today too. they were trying to tab back to the workspace picker and ended up scrolled away.
Kevin: quick win: make the banner position: sticky and overlay content instead of pushing it. then animate opacity instead of layout shift.
Elaine: overlay helps but we must ensure the banner does not obscure important controls. If it's overlaying, provide enough top padding or a visible affordance so keyboard focus isn't hidden. Also ensure screen readers still announce it via aria-live.
Maria: question: if we overlay, do we keep it in the document order where keyboard reaches it naturally?
Dylan: we can keep it in DOM order but visually position it absolute/sticky. that preserves sequential navigation while avoiding layout reflow.
Noor: small-screen copy needs shortening too. current: "Your workspace is almost ready 9 — import sample projects to get started" is too long and wraps to 3 lines on phones. Suggest: "Workspace almost ready 9 — import samples" (one line).
Kevin: implementation notes: when inserting banner, measure current scrollY and then set transform translateY for the content to visually compensate if needed. but that can get janky. better to avoid changing scrollHeight. sticky overlay + additional top inset for focused elements seems simpler.
Elaine: accessibility nit: ensure banner role=status and aria-live=polite so AT announces it; do NOT programmatically move focus unless opening a modal. Also make dismiss button reachable via keyboard and include aria-label="Close onboarding banner".
Maria: another UX thing: when a user triggers "Import sample" the UI shows a progress toast that also appears bottom-right; together with the banner it felt noisy in tests. can we consolidate feedback into the banner (e.g., show inline progress inside banner) so there's one surface?
Dylan: consolidating makes sense. banner could change state: initial -> importing -> imported success (with checkmark) and CTA toggles to "View samples". reduces competing surfaces.
Noor: from metrics POV, track CTR on "Import samples" from banner vs via empty state card. we'll need an event with source:banner/card. keep it privacy-safe.
Kevin: code sketch for sticky overlay approach:
```
// insert banner node in DOM after header to preserve tab order
const banner = document.createElement('div');
banner.setAttribute('role', 'status');
banner.setAttribute('aria-live', 'polite');
banner.className = 'onboard-banner sticky-overlay';
header.parentNode.insertBefore(banner, header.nextSibling);
// CSS: .sticky-overlay { position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 60; }
```
Dylan: design asks: make it 48px high on desktop, 56px on mobile, include an inline progress spinner and a single primary CTA. ensure color contrast for CTA >= 4.5:1 and add a high-contrast outline for keyboard focus.
Elaine: also ensure the banner dismiss state is persisted per session (not forever) so persistent dismiss doesn't block future onboarding nudges. store flag in session storage.
Maria: follow-ups: @Dylan update Figma with sticky-overlay variant + condensed copy, @Noor add telemetry event names, @Kevin prototype sticky overlay and stateful progress in staging, @Elaine write short a11y test script for mobile VoiceOver + NVDA. I'll run a quick manual test after Kevin's prototype.
